Isolated liver perfusion for non-resectable liver tumours: a review. Many treatments have been proposed for non-resectable primary or secondary hepatic cancer but the results have generally been disappointing. Isolated Hepatic Perfusion (IHP) was first attempted four decades ago but it gained acceptance only recently, after spectacular tumour responses were obtained by isolated limb perfusion with melphalan and tumour necrosis factor (TNF) for melanomas and sarcomas. Surgical isolation of the liver is a technically demanding operation that allows the safe administration of high doses of chemotherapeutics and TNF.
